steps.intent: Our primary objective is to maintain our diplomatic leadership through the U.S.-Egypt-Qatar mediation channel and ensure that any call for a ceasefire is strictly and inextricably linked to the release of all hostages, while preventing permanent territorial reduction or displacement in Gaza. The main friction points during negotiations will be resistance from Algeria, Russia, and China to linking the ceasefire to hostage release (as they favour an unconditional ceasefire), Council pressure regarding recent Israeli military expansion, and the explicit condemnation of Hamas.

messages.Algeria: Algeria cannot accept any formulation that subordinates an immediate ceasefire to conditionalities, which effectively grants the occupying Power license to persist in its campaign of slaughter, forced displacement, and territorial annexation. The Council must uphold international law without double standards and demand an unconditional, permanent ceasefire, the full withdrawal of occupation forces, and the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid, including through UNRWA. Protecting Palestinian lives from extermination is an urgent legal and moral imperative that the Council cannot continue to defer.
messages.China: China underscores that securing an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire is the overriding imperative to stop the ongoing humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. Council resolutions must not establish preconditions or artificial linkages that justify the continuation of military operations and collective punishment of civilians. Furthermore, Council language rejecting any territorial reduction of the Gaza Strip must strictly adhere to the formulation in resolution 2735 (2024) without dilution.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly welcomes the United States' initiative and broadly supports this balanced text, which rightly links an immediate ceasefire to the release of all hostages and calls for unhindered humanitarian access. To ensure consistency with Council precedent and international humanitarian law, we should strictly maintain the agreed language of resolution 2735 (2024) rejecting any reduction of Gaza's territory or creation of buffer zones without qualifiers. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder towards the swift adoption of this critical resolution.
messages.France: France welcomes this timely initiative by the United States to reinstate a durable ceasefire, secure the unconditional release of all hostages, and end the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza. We fully support the core architecture of the draft, but urge the penholder to strictly adhere to the agreed language of resolution 2735 (2024) regarding Gaza's territorial integrity by deleting 'permanently' in OP5. Reaffirming the established international parameters for the two-State solution and ensuring full protection for all humanitarian personnel are also essential to securing a robust and consensual outcome.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the initiative of the United States to revitalize the framework of Resolution 2735 (2024), secure the unconditional release of all hostages, and establish a durable ceasefire with unhindered humanitarian access. To ensure consistency with established Council language, we ask to align OP5 strictly with Resolution 2735 by rejecting any reduction of Gaza's territory, without qualifying it as 'permanent'. Greece fully supports the core architecture of the text and looks forward to its swift adoption.
messages.Guyana: Guyana appreciates the penholder's efforts to revive diplomatic momentum, but the catastrophic reality on the ground requires the Council to act decisively by demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire rather than conditioning the protection of civilian life. We must also explicitly reaffirm the indispensable role of UNRWA in Gaza's humanitarian architecture and ensure that the rejection of territorial reduction strictly mirrors the language previously agreed in resolution 2735.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan cannot accept conditioning an immediate ceasefire on other considerations; the saving of civilian lives and halting the ongoing annihilation in Gaza must be immediate and unconditional. We must not dilute international law by tolerating any territorial occupation or reduction, temporary or otherwise, nor can the Council ignore the irreplaceable mandate of UNRWA. We urge the penholder to amend the draft to reflect an unambiguous demand for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire and full respect for international humanitarian law.
messages.Panama: Panama expresses its full support for the draft resolution presented by the United States. The draft achieves an essential balance by demanding the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, calling for an urgent and durable ceasefire in line with resolution 2735, and addressing the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We commend the indispensable mediation efforts of the United States, Egypt, and Qatar, and we stand ready to support this text without reservations.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea welcomes the United States' initiative and leadership in tabling this draft resolution to break the deadlock and halt the devastating resumption of hostilities. We fully support the core objectives of achieving an immediate and durable ceasefire, securing the immediate release of all hostages, and ensuring unhindered humanitarian access at scale. To reinforce Council consistency and build broader consensus, we propose aligning the text closely with agreed language from resolutions 2728 (2024) and 2735 (2024), particularly regarding the rejection of any actions reducing the territory of Gaza.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot accept another flawed draft that conditions the cessation of hostilities on hostage negotiations, which effectively provides political cover for Israel's renewed military offensive and devastating land occupation in Gaza. The Council must fulfill its mandate by demanding an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, rather than recycling ambiguous formulations that have already failed. Unless the penholder removes all conditional linkages and introduces a clear demand for an unconditional ceasefire, we will oppose this resolution.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone appreciates the United States' initiative to re-engage the Security Council and revitalize the diplomatic framework established under resolution 2735 to halt the devastating resumption of hostilities. In light of the unbearable civilian casualties and displacement across Gaza, it is critical that Council language remains firm, particularly regarding the full territorial integrity of Gaza and the indispensable role of UN agencies, including UNRWA, in delivering life-saving relief. We stand ready to work constructively with the penholder to ensure this resolution effectively ends the carnage and secures the release of all hostages.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the penholder's initiative to re-engage the Council amid the devastating resumption of hostilities and catastrophic civilian suffering in Gaza. To uphold the Council's established acquis, the text must faithfully reflect resolution 2735 (2024) by rejecting any reduction of Gaza's territory without qualification, and by clearly demanding an immediate ceasefire and hostage release. Furthermore, we must explicitly safeguard United Nations and humanitarian personnel, particularly UNRWA, in full compliance with international humanitarian law and International Court of Justice provisional measures.
messages.Somalia: Somalia cannot accept language that makes an immediate halt to the catastrophic military operations and starvation of civilians in Gaza conditional. A permanent and immediate ceasefire is an urgent humanitarian necessity to save lives and must not be subordinated to political pretexts. We also insist on removing any qualifiers, such as 'permanently', that could legitimize ongoing land seizures, buffer zones, or the forced displacement of the Palestinian people.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom warmly welcomes the United States' leadership in tabling this draft resolution, which rightly condemns Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October, demands the unconditional release of all hostages, and anchors the path to a durable ceasefire in resolution 2735 (2024). We suggest aligning operative paragraph 5 strictly with the agreed language of resolution 2735 by deleting 'permanently', and underscoring the imperative of removing all bureaucratic and operational impediments to humanitarian aid delivery. The UK stands ready to support this text and work closely with the penholder to ensure its swift adoption.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States accommodated broad Council consensus by deleting 'permanently' and 'unauthorized' in OP5 to align strictly with resolution 2735 (2024), strengthening OP2 to 'Demands', adding references to the removal of humanitarian barriers and the protection of United Nations personnel in OP4, and reaffirming international law in OP6. However, the United States maintained its red line that any durable end to hostilities must remain inextricably linked to the immediate release of all hostages.

messages.Algeria: Algeria reiterates that the Security Council cannot subordinate an immediate halt to the massacre of Palestinian civilians to any preconditions; making a ceasefire 'inextricably linked' to hostage release grants the occupying Power a green light to continue its campaign of destruction and collective punishment. While we welcome the improvements in OP5, the Council's priority must remain the unconditional preservation of human life and adherence to the precedent of resolution 2728 (2024). Furthermore, any credible humanitarian response must explicitly protect and recognize UNRWA as the backbone of relief operations in Gaza.
messages.China: China maintains that saving civilian lives and halting the catastrophic military operations across Gaza cannot be made conditional or held hostage to ongoing negotiations. The Council's primary responsibility is to demand an immediate and durable ceasefire without creating pretexts for continued military actions and territorial occupation. If the penholder removes the conditional phrasing in OP2 and PP6, aligning the text with the imperative of upholding international humanitarian law and the spirit of resolutions 2728 and 2735, China will be able to support this draft.
messages.Denmark: Denmark thanks the United States for accommodating our proposals in Revision 1, particularly regarding the preservation of Gaza's territorial integrity and the explicit adherence to international humanitarian law. We view the current text as balanced, robust, and essential for achieving an immediate and durable ceasefire inextricably linked to the release of all hostages, as well as guaranteeing unimpeded humanitarian access. Denmark fully supports the draft as presented and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France commends the United States for accommodating our comments in revision 1, particularly by aligning OP5 with resolution 2735 (2024) and explicitly protecting United Nations personnel in OP4. The draft strikes an essential balance by demanding an immediate ceasefire inextricably linked to the release of all hostages, ensuring large-scale humanitarian access, and upholding the path toward a two-State solution. France is fully prepared to vote in favor of this resolution as drafted.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals into Revision 1, notably ensuring full consistency with resolution 2735 regarding territorial integrity and explicitly safeguarding United Nations personnel. The current text strikes a necessary and responsible balance, demanding an immediate ceasefire inextricably linked to the release of all hostages, guaranteeing unhindered humanitarian access, and upholding the two-State solution. Greece fully supports this draft and stands ready to vote in favor.
messages.Guyana: Guyana appreciates the penholder's incorporation of our proposal in operative paragraph 5 and the strengthening of operative paragraph 2 to a demand. However, a sustainable humanitarian response is impossible without explicitly recognizing the indispensable mandate of UNRWA, and international humanitarian law does not permit conditioning an end to the catastrophic killing of civilians. We urge the penholder to address these essential elements to ensure the Council delivers an effective, principled response.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan reiterates that international humanitarian law does not permit conditioning an end to the slaughter and starvation of civilians on any political or reciprocal criteria; retaining 'inextricably linked' effectively grants a pretext for the ongoing military campaign and collective punishment. We urge the penholder to bring the text in line with the established Council balance in resolutions 2728 and 2735. Furthermore, explicit recognition of UNRWA's indispensable lifeline in OP4 remains vital given the catastrophic conditions on the ground.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the revised draft resolution as presented. The text strikes a necessary and principled balance by explicitly condemning terrorism, demanding the immediate release of all hostages, securing unhindered humanitarian relief, and charting a realistic path toward a durable ceasefire through the established mediation framework. We appreciate the penholder's leadership and stand ready to vote in favor of this resolution.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea appreciates the penholder's constructive engagement and the full incorporation of our proposals into revision 1, notably strengthening OP2 to demand an immediate ceasefire and aligning OP5 with agreed Council language. We believe this balanced text effectively addresses the critical imperatives of ending hostilities, securing the release of all hostages, and scaling up humanitarian assistance. The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution as currently formulated and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot accept language that conditions an end to the bloodshed on hostage releases, effectively giving Israel a free hand to continue its devastating military campaign against Palestinian civilians. The Security Council must demand an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire, rather than recycling failed and ambiguous formulas from resolution 2735. If the penholder maintains this inherently flawed and conditional approach, Russia will not be able to support this draft and will vote against it.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone expresses sincere appreciation to the penholder for incorporating our key recommendations, particularly upgrading operative paragraph 2 to demand a ceasefire and upholding the territorial integrity of Gaza in operative paragraph 5 without qualification. In light of the dire humanitarian catastrophe on the ground, we urge the inclusion of an explicit reference to UNRWA, whose operational role remains indispensable for delivering life-saving relief at scale. Sierra Leone remains committed to supporting this text to bring about an immediate cessation of hostilities, secure the release of all hostages, and alleviate civilian suffering.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia appreciates the penholder's positive response to our requests, notably the upgrade to a clear demand for a ceasefire in operative paragraph 2 and the necessary adjustments in operative paragraph 5. We stand ready to support this draft resolution and urge its swift adoption to halt the catastrophic renewed hostilities. We make one final appeal to explicitly acknowledge the indispensable role and protection of UNRWA in operative paragraph 4.
messages.Somalia: Somalia appreciates the penholder's accommodation of our concerns regarding territorial integrity, buffer zones, and forced displacement in operative paragraph 5. Nevertheless, we cannot accept language in OP2 and PP6 that effectively conditions an end to the ongoing devastation and civilian slaughter exclusively on hostage releases without reciprocal address of Palestinian detainees. Furthermore, given the catastrophic humanitarian crisis, the text must explicitly acknowledge the indispensable mandate and operations of the United Nations, particularly UNRWA.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States for incorporating our amendments into revision 1, which strikes the necessary balance by inextricably linking an immediate ceasefire to the release of all hostages while demanding the immediate removal of all barriers to humanitarian aid. The draft firmly upholds international humanitarian law, rejects any territorial reduction or forced displacement in Gaza, and reinforces the path toward a two-State solution. The United Kingdom fully supports this text and is prepared to vote in favour.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States deleted PP6 and restructured OP2 to demand both an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire and the immediate release of all hostages in accordance with resolutions 2728 and 2735, resolving red lines raised by China, Algeria, Pakistan, and Somalia. Operative paragraph 4 was updated to explicitly safeguard United Nations personnel, including UNRWA, and operative paragraph 1 now references arbitrarily detained persons. These adjustments maintain core United States national interests and diplomatic efforts while averting any permanent member veto, yielding a projected 14-0-1 adoption with the Russian Federation abstaining.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria votes in favour as the penholder addressed our core concerns and red lines by removing conditional linking language, aligning OP2 with resolutions 2728 and 2735, explicitly referencing UNRWA, and addressing arbitrarily detained persons, all in service of our overriding priority to end the ongoing onslaught in Gaza. Following our customary Council practice, our delegation will deliver our explanation of vote after the adoption.
reasons.China: The United States accepted all of China's proposed amendments, including removing conditional linkages between the ceasefire and hostage releases and addressing arbitrary detention, while the text firmly demands an immediate ceasefire, humanitarian access, and rejects any territorial reduction or displacement in Gaza.
reasons.Denmark: The draft resolution aligns fully with Denmark's foreign policy priorities and EU consensus: demanding the release of hostages, condemning Hamas's terrorism, establishing an immediate ceasefire, protecting civilians and UN/humanitarian workers (including UNRWA), upholding international humanitarian law, rejecting territorial or demographic changes to Gaza, and reaffirming the two-State solution. Having supported the draft during negotiations, Denmark votes in favour.
reasons.France: The draft resolution aligns fully with France's long-standing positions by demanding an immediate and durable ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access including support for UNRWA, and reaffirming the two-State solution; in line with its established practice, France reserves its remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution as it strikes the necessary balance by demanding an immediate ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, unimpeded humanitarian access, and adherence to international humanitarian law while firmly upholding the two-State solution.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana votes in favour because the draft resolution demands an immediate and durable ceasefire, humanitarian access at scale, explicit recognition of UNRWA, and firmly rejects any territorial reduction or forced displacement in Gaza, addressing our key national priorities. We reserve our remarks for an explanation of vote following the adoption.
reasons.Pakistan: The United States addressed our primary red lines by removing language conditioning a ceasefire on hostage releases, aligning the text with resolutions 2728 and 2735, and explicitly referencing UNRWA. Given the urgent need to halt the catastrophic renewed hostilities in Gaza, reject forced displacement, and secure unhindered humanitarian access, Pakistan votes in favour.
reasons.Panama: Panama consistently supports balanced diplomatic initiatives that demand the unconditional release of all hostages, call for an immediate ceasefire, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and reaffirm commitment to a negotiated two-State solution. As the draft resolution submitted by the United States addresses these critical priorities and reflects our position during negotiations, Panama votes in favour.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The draft resolution aligns with the Republic of Korea's consistent stance demanding an immediate and durable ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance, while maintaining strong alignment with our ally, the United States, as the penholder.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia cannot vote in favour of a US-drafted resolution that glorifies flawed Western diplomacy and ties the ceasefire to the failed resolution 2735 framework rather than demanding an unconditional, permanent ceasefire. However, because the text explicitly demands an immediate ceasefire and humanitarian access, vetoing it would diplomatically isolate Russia from the Arab Group and elected members, making abstention the consistent choice as seen in resolution 2735.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone consistently votes in favour of Security Council draft resolutions demanding an immediate ceasefire, the release of hostages, and unimpeded humanitarian assistance at scale, and its specific negotiation request explicitly protecting UNRWA was incorporated into the text. Following its established Council practice, Sierra Leone will deliver any explanation of vote after the adoption process.
reasons.Slovenia: The draft resolution incorporates Slovenia's key priorities, including a clear demand for an immediate and durable ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid, explicit protection for UNRWA, and the rejection of territorial changes or forced displacement. Slovenia therefore votes in favour, in line with its consistent record of upholding international law and Council unity.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia votes in favour as the revised draft resolution incorporates crucial elements, including demanding an immediate and durable ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian assistance with explicit recognition of UNRWA, and a clear rejection of forced displacement and territorial changes in Gaza.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft resolution aligns fully with United Kingdom foreign policy by demanding an immediate and durable ceasefire, the unconditional release of all hostages, the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid, and an explicit condemnation of the 7 October Hamas terrorist attacks, alongside rejecting any territorial reduction or displacement in Gaza.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and sponsor of the draft resolution, the United States votes in favour to advance its diplomatic framework linking an immediate ceasefire to the release of all hostages, ensure sustained humanitarian relief, and reject any permanent territorial or demographic alterations to Gaza.

before.Denmark:
Mr. President, 

Denmark will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us today. 

The catastrophic situation in Gaza and the renewed escalation of hostilities demand urgent, decisive, and united action by this Council. The suffering of civilians has reached intolerable levels, and the breakdown of the cessation of hostilities has only deepened the humanitarian tragedy. 

This draft resolution strikes the necessary and principled balance. It unequivocally condemns the horrific terrorist attacks of 7 October by Hamas and demands the immediate, unconditional release of all remaining hostages. At the same time, it rightly demands an immediate and durable ceasefire, full compliance by all parties with international humanitarian law, and the safe, unimpeded delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale, ensuring the protection of United Nations personnel, including UNRWA, and all humanitarian workers.

Crucially, the resolution firmly rejects any demographic or territorial alteration of the Gaza Strip, including forced displacement, which is strictly prohibited under international law. It underscores that lasting peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians can only be achieved through a negotiated two-State solution, with Gaza and the West Bank unified under the Palestinian Authority.

We commend the ongoing diplomatic mediation led by the United States, Egypt, and Qatar. It is imperative that the Council speaks with one voice to support these efforts and alleviate the immense suffering on the ground. We urge all members to support this resolution.

Thank you.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation cannot support the draft resolution prepared by the United States delegation. 

Once again, Washington is attempting to sell the Council a cosmetic product designed not to genuinely stop the Israeli military machine, but to provide diplomatic cover for its continued actions on the ground. The reality in Gaza is catastrophic: the ceasefire reached earlier this year was unilaterally shattered, leading to thousands more civilian casualties and renewed efforts to displace the population and seize land. Yet the American text continues to chain the Council to the bankrupt framework of resolution 2735, which has already proven completely ineffective. 

Instead of an unambiguous, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire demanded by the overwhelming majority of the international community, we are presented with convoluted formulations and unwarranted praise for American mediation that has yielded zero tangible protection for Palestinians. We repeatedly proposed clear, unequivocal language demanding an unconditional and permanent cessation of hostilities and a complete withdrawal of Israeli forces. These demands were disregarded. 

At the same time, because the draft does contain a direct demand for a ceasefire and calls for humanitarian access and the protection of UNRWA, we will not block it, out of respect for our Arab partners and the elected members of the Council. The Russian Federation will therefore abstain.
before.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States has brought this draft resolution before the Security Council today because the situation in Gaza demands decisive, responsible leadership and clear action from this body. Following the deeply concerning collapse of the earlier cessation of hostilities and the catastrophic escalation of military operations, we cannot afford inaction or complacency. Civilians in Gaza are enduring unimaginable suffering, and dozens of hostages—including American citizens—remain cruelly held by Hamas under horrific conditions after nearly twenty months of captivity.

This resolution addresses the crisis directly and realistically. It firmly links an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire to the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, reaffirming the indispensable framework established under resolutions 2728 and 2735. It makes clear that Hamas cannot be allowed to hold hostages with impunity, while demanding an immediate surge and unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale across the entirety of Gaza. 

Crucially, this text rejects any demographic or territorial reduction of Gaza, rejects forced displacement, and reiterates our unwavering commitment to the two-State solution, with Gaza and the West Bank unified under a reformed Palestinian Authority. Together with our partners in Egypt and Qatar, the United States has worked tirelessly to negotiate a diplomatic path out of this devastating conflict. This Council must speak with one voice to reinforce those diplomatic efforts, save civilian lives, and bring every single hostage home. We urge every member of this Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

Thank you.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

We did so guided by one single, unwavering principle that has defined our mandate in this Council: the preservation of Palestinian lives and the urgent necessity to halt the ongoing massacre, devastation, and starvation inflicted upon the Palestinian people in Gaza. 

For nearly twenty months, the international community has witnessed an unprecedented campaign of collective punishment, mass slaughter, and deliberate destruction. When the ceasefire broke down in March, the occupying Power resumed its brutal military aggression with even greater ferocity, killing thousands more innocent civilians, targeting shelters, and attempting once again to forcibly displace the Palestinian population and annex their land. 

Today, this Council has demanded an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire. It has demanded the unimpeded delivery of life-saving humanitarian aid at scale through all crossings. It has unequivocally reaffirmed the vital and irreplaceable role of UNRWA, and it has categorically rejected any demographic or territorial change, buffer zones, or the forced displacement of Palestinians from their ancestral land. 

These demands are not optional. They are binding under international law and the United Nations Charter. The Security Council cannot tolerate yet another resolution being treated as mere paper to be ignored and trampled upon by the Israeli occupying forces. The Council’s credibility is on the line. 

While we voted in favour of this resolution to give peace and human survival a chance, we must be absolutely clear: this text is only a step. A ceasefire must not be a temporary pause to be broken at will, nor a cover for continued colonial occupation. Lasting peace in the Middle East can never be achieved through the illusion of managing occupation or through the barrel of a gun. It requires addressing the root cause: ending the illegal occupation of all Palestinian and Arab lands, upholding the inalienable rights of the heroic Palestinian people, including their right to self-determination and the establishment of their independent, fully sovereign State with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.

Algeria will never abandon the Palestinian people in their just struggle for freedom and dignity. We expect this resolution to be implemented immediately and fully, without preconditions or delay. 

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just adopted. 

For nearly twenty months, the conflict in Gaza has caused an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. Tens of thousands of innocent civilians, the vast majority of them women and children, have lost their lives, and more than two million people have been plunged into utter devastation, displacement, and despair. The breakdown of the earlier ceasefire and the renewed, intensified military offensives since March have once again pushed the people of Gaza to the brink of survival. UN experts have warned of the total destruction facing Gaza's population. This ongoing tragedy tests the conscience of humanity and the credibility of this Council.

China has consistently and unequivocally called for an immediate, durable, and unconditional ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and arbitrarily detained persons, the protection of civilians, and the full, unimpeded entry of humanitarian assistance. In light of the urgent need to halt the fighting, save innocent lives, and alleviate the humanitarian disaster, China cast a positive vote.

Today’s resolution clearly demands an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access at scale, and the protection of United Nations agencies, including UNRWA, and humanitarian personnel. It also explicitly rejects any demographic or territorial changes in Gaza, the creation of buffer zones, and the forced displacement of civilians. These are not merely political calls; they are non-negotiable obligations under international law and international humanitarian law. Security Council resolutions are legally binding on all Member States under the Charter of the United Nations. The parties concerned, especially Israel as the occupying power, must immediately cease all military operations, effectively implement this resolution without delay or preconditions, and end the collective punishment of the Palestinian people. 

We must also emphasize that a temporary pause cannot be a substitute for lasting peace, nor should diplomatic negotiations become an excuse for delaying the cessation of hostilities on the ground. We urge the countries with significant influence to act in an objective, just, and responsible manner, to abandon double standards, and to take tangible actions to ensure that the Council’s resolutions are fully respected and executed.

The fundamental solution to the question of Palestine lies in the implementation of the two-State solution, the end of the illegal occupation, and the restoration of the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people, including the establishment of an independent State of Palestine based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital. China will continue to work tirelessly with the international community to bring an immediate end to the conflict in Gaza, restore peace and stability, and achieve a just, comprehensive, and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France welcomes the adoption of this resolution and voted in favour of the text presented by the United States. 

Faced with the renewed escalation of violence and the catastrophic, intolerable humanitarian tragedy unfolding in the Gaza Strip, the Security Council had the duty to act and make its voice heard clearly and firmly. 

First and foremost, France reiterates its demand for an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire. The resumption of intense military operations and the intolerable civilian death toll must end. International humanitarian law must be strictly respected by all parties, at all times and in all places. The protection of civilians, humanitarian personnel, and medical infrastructure is an absolute obligation from which there can be no derogation.

France once again condemns in the strongest possible terms the heinous terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas and other groups on 7 October 2023. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Their continued captivity after twenty months of anguish is unacceptable and intolerable for their families and loved ones. 

Humanitarian assistance must be allowed to enter Gaza safely, unhindered, and at scale, through all available crossings. In this regard, France underscores the indispensable, irreplaceable role of the United Nations and its agencies, particularly UNRWA, whose personnel carry out life-saving work under perilous conditions and must be fully protected. 

Furthermore, France firmly rejects any attempts at demographic or territorial changes in the Gaza Strip, any establishment of buffer zones, or any forced displacement of the Palestinian population. The Gaza Strip is Palestinian land, and its future lies as an integral part of a unified Palestinian State. 

Finally, as this Council has repeatedly reaffirmed, there can be no lasting peace without a political perspective. The only viable path forward remains the two-State solution, with two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognized borders, with Gaza and the West Bank unified under the Palestinian Authority. France will continue to spare no effort, together with its partners, to translate this vision into reality.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Greece:
Mr. President,

Greece voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Security Council. 

Our vote reflects Greece’s steadfast and principled foreign policy, anchored in full respect for the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and international humanitarian law. 

The catastrophic situation in Gaza and the recent breakdown of the cessation of hostilities have brought further immense suffering to innocent civilians. This cycle of violence must end. Today’s adoption sends a clear, unified message from the Council on the urgent steps required to de-escalate the crisis and alleviate human suffering.

First, we reiterate our unequivocal condemnation of all acts of terrorism, including the heinous attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October 2023. We demand the immediate, unconditional, and dignified release of all remaining hostages, whose prolonged captivity remains an intolerable anguish for their families.

Second, the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza demands immediate, bold, and sustained action. The delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale, safely and unhindered through all crossings, is an absolute moral and legal imperative. The protection of civilians, humanitarian and medical personnel, and United Nations staff and facilities—including UNRWA—must be ensured at all times by all parties in strict compliance with international humanitarian law.

Third, Greece firmly opposes any forced displacement of the civilian population, as well as any demographic or territorial changes in the Gaza Strip. The territorial integrity of Gaza is non-negotiable.

We commend the tireless diplomatic mediation led by the United States, Egypt, and Qatar, and we urge all parties to implement the terms of this resolution in good faith, restore the phased ceasefire framework, and move decisively toward a permanent cessation of hostilities.

Finally, we must not lose sight of the political horizon. True and lasting security for both Israelis and Palestinians can only be achieved through a revitalized political process leading to a negotiated two-State solution, in line with relevant Security Council resolutions, with the Gaza Strip and the West Bank unified under the legitimate authority of the Palestinian Authority. Greece stands ready to support all efforts to turn this vision into reality.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Guyana:
Mr. President,

Guyana voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We did so out of a profound sense of responsibility and an acute awareness of the desperate, catastrophic reality facing civilians in the Gaza Strip.

For nearly twenty months, the Palestinian civilian population has been subjected to unimaginable horrors, relentless bombardment, mass displacement, and acute deprivation. The resumption of intense military operations and the collapse of the previous cessation of hostilities have only deepened this humanitarian catastrophe, pushing an already devastated population to the brink of complete ruin. 

Guyana has consistently maintained that this Council cannot remain silent in the face of such immense human suffering. We voted in favour of this text because it demands what is most urgently needed: an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, and the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages. 

We also welcome the clear provisions in the resolution demanding the immediate, safe, and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance at scale throughout Gaza, and explicitly recognizing the indispensable, life-saving role of United Nations agencies, particularly UNRWA. Humanitarian assistance must never be politicized or used as a weapon of war, and the safety of humanitarian personnel and infrastructure must be fully respected in accordance with international humanitarian law.

Furthermore, Guyana firmly supports paragraph 5 of the resolution, which unequivocally rejects any attempts at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip, including the creation of buffer zones and the forced displacement of civilians. Gaza is, and must remain, an integral part of Palestinian territory.

Mr. President, 

The adoption of this resolution is an important step, but words on paper alone will not save lives. Security Council resolutions are legally binding under international law and demand full, immediate, and unconditional implementation by all parties. The continuous cycle of bloodshed must end. The parties must immediately silence the guns, return all remaining hostages to their families, and recommit in good faith to a political process aimed at achieving a just, lasting, and comprehensive peace based on the two-State solution, with the States of Israel and Palestine living side by side within secure and recognized borders.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Security Council. We did so out of a profound sense of urgency and moral responsibility in the face of the ongoing tragedy in Gaza. 

For nearly twenty months, the world has witnessed unprecedented death, devastation, and human suffering inflicted upon the besieged Palestinian people. The breakdown of the earlier cessation of hostilities in March and the subsequent relentless military operations have unleashed further catastrophe upon a civilian population that has already endured unimaginable horrors. Tens of thousands of innocent civilians—predominantly women and children—have been killed, infrastructure has been systematically destroyed, and millions have been pushed to the brink of starvation and disease. 

Today’s resolution reflects the minimum necessary response of this Council. Silence or paralysis in the face of such carnage is unacceptable. By adopting this text, the Council has sent a clear and unequivocal message: the hostilities must cease immediately, unconditionally, and permanently. An immediate, full, and durable ceasefire is imperative to save lives, allow humanitarian assistance to reach all those in desperate need, and secure the release of all hostages and arbitrarily detained persons. 

Pakistan welcomes the resolution’s explicit rejection of any attempt at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip. Any measures aimed at seizing land, establishing buffer zones, reducing the territory of Gaza, or forcibly displacing the Palestinian population constitute flagrant violations of international law, the UN Charter, and the Fourth Geneva Convention. Such actions are illegal, unacceptable, and must be firmly resisted.

We also underline the vital, irreplaceable role of the United Nations, particularly UNRWA, in providing life-saving relief and sustenance to millions of Palestinian refugees. The siege must be lifted, all crossing points opened, and all obstacles to the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid dismantled immediately. Humanitarian workers and medical facilities must be protected at all times.

Mr. President, 

While this resolution is an important step, we must recognize that a durable peace cannot be achieved through temporary arrangements or by freezing an unjust status quo. Nor can peace be built on the continued subjugation and disenfranchisement of an entire people. The root cause of this conflict is the prolonged and illegal Israeli occupation of Palestinian territories. 

True security and lasting stability in the Middle East can only be realized through the exercise of the Palestinian people’s inalienable right to self-determination. This requires the establishment of a viable, sovereign, and contiguous State of Palestine, based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. 

Pakistan calls upon the Security Council to ensure the full and immediate implementation of the resolution adopted today and to hold accountable those who continue to violate international law and the decisions of this body.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Panama:
Mr. President,

Panama voted in favour of the resolution just adopted by the Security Council. 

My delegation’s vote reflects our steadfast commitment to the principles of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and international humanitarian law, as well as our conviction that this Council must act decisively to alleviate the catastrophic humanitarian tragedy in the Gaza Strip.

The resumption of hostilities and the continued loss of innocent civilian lives, particularly among women and children, is deeply distressing. Civilians must never be the target of military operations, and international humanitarian law must be respected under all circumstances. It is imperative that humanitarian assistance reach all those in need rapidly, safely, and at scale, through all available crossing points, and that humanitarian and medical personnel be protected at all times.

Panama reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of all acts of terrorism, including the heinous attacks of 7 October 2023. We reiterate our firm demand for the immediate, unconditional, and dignified release of all remaining hostages still held in Gaza, whose prolonged captivity is unacceptable. 

We welcome that this resolution demands an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, inextricably linked to the release of all hostages, and urges the parties to return in good faith to the negotiating table. We commend and fully support the tireless diplomatic mediation efforts carried out by Egypt, Qatar, and the United States to reinstate a phased agreement that puts an end to the hostilities.

Furthermore, Panama categorically rejects any attempt at demographic or territorial alteration in the Gaza Strip, as well as the forced displacement of the Palestinian population, which violates international humanitarian law.

Finally, Panama reaffirms its unwavering commitment to a just, lasting, and peaceful resolution to the conflict through the two-State solution, where two democratic States, Israel and Palestine, live side by side in peace, security, and dignity within secure and recognized borders, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Korea voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

We welcome the Council’s decisive action today. The breakdown of the cessation of hostilities and the dramatic escalation of military operations over the past several months have plunged Gaza into an even deeper humanitarian catastrophe. Innocent civilians have paid an unbearable price, while dozens of hostages continue to endure unimaginable agony after nearly twenty months of captivity. 

Under these dire circumstances, the Council could not remain silent. This resolution sends a clear, united, and balanced message: it demands an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale throughout the Gaza Strip. 

We commend the United States for penning this text and thank the mediators—the United States, Egypt, and Qatar—for their tireless and dedicated diplomatic efforts. We urge both parties to immediately re-engage in good faith within this framework to reinstate the ceasefire and achieve a permanent end to hostilities. 

My delegation also underscores the vital importance of paragraph 5 of the resolution. International humanitarian law must be strictly upheld. Any attempt at demographic or territorial change in Gaza, including the creation of buffer zones or the forced displacement of civilians, is unacceptable and must be rejected. 

Furthermore, full, rapid, and unimpeded humanitarian access must be ensured without delay. The safety and security of all humanitarian and medical personnel, including the United Nations and its agencies, must be fully respected and protected. 

Mr. President,

As we have consistently emphasized in this chamber, adopting a resolution is not the end of our responsibility; it is only the beginning. Words alone cannot alleviate the suffering of innocent civilians or bring the hostages home. The measures demanded in this resolution must be fully and faithfully implemented on the ground without delay. 

Ultimately, lasting peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians can only be realized through a negotiated two-State solution, where two democratic States live side by side in peace and security within recognized borders. The Republic of Korea remains steadfast in its commitment to supporting all international efforts toward that objective.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Sierra Leone:
Mr. President,

Sierra Leone voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

We thank the United States for its initiative and leadership in penning this resolution, as well as all Council members for their constructive engagement. We also once again commend and express our full support for the sustained diplomatic efforts spearheaded by Egypt, Qatar, and the United States aimed at de-escalating the crisis, achieving a lasting ceasefire, and securing the release of hostages.

Sierra Leone’s vote today is guided by our principled and consistent position that the Security Council must act decisively to uphold international peace and security, protect civilian lives, and end the catastrophic suffering in the Gaza Strip. The resumption of intense military operations following the breakdown of the earlier cessation of hostilities has only deepened the horrors endured by the civilian population, who continue to bear the unbearable brunt of this conflict, with women and children disproportionately affected.

We voted in favour of this text because it demands an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and the unimpeded delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance at scale throughout Gaza. In the face of catastrophic humanitarian conditions and near-total collapse of essential services, aid must reach all those in desperate need through all available crossings without hindrance or delay. In this regard, we reiterate our steadfast support for the vital and irreplaceable role played by the United Nations, particularly UNRWA, and call for the full protection of all humanitarian and medical personnel.

Sierra Leone reaffirms its firm rejection of any attempts at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip, including the creation of buffer zones or any forced displacement of Palestinians, which constitutes a clear violation of international humanitarian law.

Adopting this resolution is a vital step, but its true value lies in its full and immediate implementation by all parties. We urge Israel and Hamas to abide by the Council’s decision, comply strictly with their obligations under international law, and re-engage in negotiations in good faith.

In conclusion, Mr. President, lasting peace and security cannot be attained through military means. It can only be realized through a revitalized political process leading to a viable two-State solution, based on the 1967 borders, with the Gaza Strip unified with the West Bank under the legitimate authority of the Palestinian Authority, allowing Israelis and Palestinians to live side by side in peace and security.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Mr. President,

Slovenia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We thank the United States, as the penholder, for its efforts to bring this text forward and build Council consensus.

Since taking our seat on the Security Council, Slovenia has consistently called for a united, clear, and resolute voice from this organ. Today, with the catastrophic breakdown of the cessation of hostilities and the horrific resumption of military operations in Gaza, that voice was needed more than ever. Civilians in Gaza have endured twenty months of unimaginable devastation, starvation, loss, and displacement, while families of hostages remain in agonizing limbo. The cycle of despair must end.

Today’s resolution establishes clear demands: an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire; the immediate and unconditional release of all remaining hostages; and the unhindered flow of humanitarian aid at scale throughout the entirety of Gaza. 

International law is not optional. It is binding on all parties, at all times, without exception. Hostage-taking, attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, the denial of humanitarian access, and attacks on humanitarian workers are all grave violations of international humanitarian law. We particularly welcome the resolution's explicit recognition of the indispensable role of the United Nations, including UNRWA, whose personnel continue to perform life-saving work under perilous conditions.

Furthermore, Slovenia firmly reiterates that any attempt at demographic or territorial change in the Gaza Strip—including the establishment of buffer zones, military occupation, or the forced displacement of the civilian population—is unacceptable and strictly prohibited under international law. Gaza is an integral part of the occupied Palestinian territory.

Adopting a resolution is not enough; its true value lies in implementation on the ground. We call on both parties to immediately adhere to their obligations, re-engage in good faith through the mediation of Egypt, Qatar, and the United States, and turn this resolution into reality.

Ultimately, lasting peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians cannot be achieved through military means. It can only be secured through a political horizon: a viable, sovereign State of Palestine living side by side in peace and security with the State of Israel, within secure and recognized borders. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Somalia:
Mr. President,

Somalia voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

We did so out of a profound sense of responsibility and urgency. For nearly twenty months, the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip have endured unspeakable horrors, catastrophic loss of life, widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure, and the looming threat of famine and forced displacement. The resumption of intense military operations and the breakdown of the previous cessation of hostilities have brought human suffering to an intolerable peak. This bloodshed must end immediately.

Somalia welcomes the Council’s demand for an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire. A ceasefire is not merely a political necessity; it is a moral imperative to save lives. It is critical that all parties fully comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The safe, unhindered, and sustained delivery of humanitarian aid at scale must be guaranteed through all crossings without impediment. In this regard, we reaffirm our full support for the vital and irreplaceable mandate of UNRWA and salute the courageous humanitarian and medical personnel operating under perilous conditions.

We also welcome the resolution’s unequivocal rejection of any demographic or territorial changes in the Gaza Strip, including any reduction of territory, the creation of buffer zones, or the forced displacement of Palestinians, which constitutes a grave violation of international law. Gaza is an integral part of the occupied Palestinian territory.

Mr. President,

While this resolution is an important and necessary step, Council resolutions must not remain ink on paper. We call for its immediate, full, and unconditional implementation by all parties. 

Ultimately, durable peace and security can only be achieved by addressing the root causes of the conflict through an end to the occupation and the realization of the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people. Somalia reaffirms its steadfast support for the two-State solution, envisioning an independent, sovereign, and viable State of Palestine living side by side in peace and security with Israel, based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations resolutions and the Arab Peace Initiative.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution. We welcome its adoption by this Council at a critical moment for the people of Gaza, the region, and the remaining hostages and their families.

The renewed escalation of fighting and the breakdown of the earlier cessation of hostilities have brought yet further devastation and unimaginable suffering to civilians in Gaza. Tens of thousands of innocent Palestinians have lost their lives, famine and disease loom, and basic human dignity is being stripped away. This catastrophe cannot be allowed to continue.

That is why the United Kingdom has consistently called for an immediate, full, and durable ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and an urgent, massive surge in humanitarian assistance across Gaza. 

This resolution sets out those imperatives clearly. It unequivocally condemns the horrific terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October 2023 and demands the release of all remaining hostages, who have now endured nearly twenty months of brutal captivity. Israel has the right to defend its citizens against terrorism, but that right must be exercised strictly in line with international humanitarian law. Far too many civilians have been killed. 

Aid must flow rapidly, safely, and unhindered through all crossings, and the barriers currently impeding humanitarian delivery must be lifted immediately. Humanitarian and medical workers, who risk their lives daily, as well as United Nations personnel and facilities, must be protected.

The resolution also sends an unambiguous message: there must be no territorial reduction of Gaza, no permanent buffer zones, and no forced displacement of its population. The Gaza Strip must remain an integral part of Palestinian territory, unified with the West Bank under a revitalised Palestinian Authority.

We commend the tireless diplomatic efforts of the United States, Qatar, and Egypt. We urge both parties to return immediately to the negotiating table in good faith and implement this framework in full. 

Ultimately, military action alone will not deliver enduring security for Israel nor dignity and statehood for Palestinians. We must use this resolution as a foundation to establish an irreversible pathway towards a two-State solution, where a secure and safe Israel lives alongside a viable and sovereign Palestinian State. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
